subject: PrivDeploy GPU pool — lane-driven scaling roadmap and pilot
messages:
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: infra-lead@oraedge.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PrivDeploy GPU pool capacity kickoff / info request

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Following up with a concise kickoff so we can scope the private GPU pool sizing and a short pilot for OraEdge. Goal: define throughput targets, latency bands, and an initial lane allocation that meets your SLA windows while keeping egress and batch economics explicit.

Key asks (please send the numbers if you have them, or the closest estimate):
- Typical traffic mix across models (percent split by model family, e.g., small chat, long-context summarization).
- Sustained QPS and 99th/95th token latency targets per workload. We usually plan for sustained + 3x short burst.
- Burst profile: typical burst concurrency (RPS) and max burst duration in minutes.
- Networking constraints: uplink per rack (100G/200G), expected cross-AZ egress rate, and whether you plan to oversubscribe NICs.
- Compliance lanes (PII) or dedicated encryption zones that must be isolated.

We typically propose a lane-driven sizing approach: 1) latency-sensitive lane (low batch, guaranteed pods), 2) cost-efficient lane (high batch, relaxed latency), 3) reserved compliance lane (isolated, pinned). We'll draft numbers once we get your traffic profile.

Attached is a short worksheet with the fields that help us run the sizing calc. If you can return it by midday PT Friday, we can share a candidate lane allocation and network egress model for your review next week.

Attachments: initial-capacity-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet, traffic worksheet)

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Product Manager — Private Deploy
Redwood Inference

From: infra-lead@oraedge.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy GPU pool capacity kickoff / info request

Hi Rishi —

Thanks — see inline answers and an attached summary from our infra team. Quick notes:
- Model mix (80/20 split): 70% small chat models (~1–2k tokens/session), 20% mid-length summarization (5–10k tokens), 10% long-retain retrieval-augmented workflows (15–40k tokens).
- Sustained throughput: 1,200 concurrent sessions average (approx 180k tokens/min sustained). Peak bursts: up to 6k sessions (~900k tokens/min) for ~10–20 minutes, usually during nightly batch windows or marketing spikes.
- Latency targets: 95th token latency target for chat: <= 300ms; 99th <= 600ms for lane A. Lane B (batch) 95th <= 1200ms acceptable.
- Networking: 2x100G per rack (dual-port), spine-leaf with 1:3 oversubscription at leaf. Cross-AZ egress capped by our cloud tenancy at 30 Gbps average with bursts to 250 Gbps.
- Compliance: we need a physically isolated lane for PII workloads with its own KMS and audit logging — likely 1–2 pinned pods initially.

Attached: oraedge-infra-summary.pdf (network diagrams) and our completed rows in the worksheet.

Questions for you:
1) How do you handle KV-cache warmup for lane B to prevent cold-start penalties when scaling?
2) For pinned compliance pods, is there an ops-friendly way to pre-warm quantized model artifacts without creating extra egress costs?

Thanks,
Priya Kaur
Head of Infrastructure — OraEdge
infra-lead@oraedge.com

Attachment: oraedge-infra-summary.pdf (network diagram), filled-in worksheet

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: infra-lead@oraedge.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-02T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy GPU pool capacity kickoff / info request

Priya —

Appreciate the detail — that profile is very helpful. Based on your numbers I sketched a lane-driven proposal and a lightweight pilot cadence. Summary below; attached are the lane CSV and a short network egress model for cost/throughput tradeoffs.

High-level lane allocation (candidate):
- Lane A (low-latency, guaranteed capacity): 20% of pool compute, kept at low-batch size (batch size 1–4), admission control with priority queuing. Targets: sustain 95th token latency <= 300ms; modeled for 250k tokens/min sustained and 600k tokens/min burst headroom.
- Lane B (throughput-optimized): 60% of pool, high batching, async KV-cache preload on warm pool; batch size tuned per model family. Targets: sustain cost-efficient throughput ~500k tokens/min with burst absorbable to 1.2M tokens/min for 15–20m windows.
- Lane C (compliance/pinned): 20% pinned nodes (1–2 pods to start) with isolated networking and HSM/KMS. Pre-warm strategy: replicate quantized artifacts to local SSDs during off-peak and run scheduled warmup requests (small synthetic prefixes) to populate KV-cache; this avoids egress during warmups if artifacts and warmers are local.

Network and NIC recommendations:
- Keep dual 100G uplinks and avoid >2:1 oversubscription for Lane A spine-to-leaf. For Lane B we can tolerate 3:1 at leaf with aggressive batching.
- Enable per-lane egress policing at the leaf to prevent background replication from stomping latency-sensitive flows.

Autoscale & warm-pool behavior:
- Warm pool size: keep enough warm pods to cover median burst-to-peak delta (~30% additional pods). Warm pool should run a lightweight warmup task that touches KV cache and quantized weights.
- Admission control: implement token-based admission where lane A gets guaranteed token slots; lane B operates on best-effort with preemption rules during severe contention.

Pilot plan (2 weeks):
1) Stage: provision a 12-GPU sandbox subdivided into lanes matching the split above.
2) Run synthetic and recorded-traffic replay for three 4-hour runs to validate 95/99 latencies and egress shaping.
3) Instrument real-time dashboards (per-route latency, token cost, KV-cache hit rate) and run a dry failover to Hosted API variant if target latency degrades beyond thresholds.

Open questions for scoping the pilot:
- Acceptance criteria for pilot pass/fail (we propose: Lane A 95th token latency <= 350ms across replay, KV-cache hit rate >= 85% for B workloads).
- Any regulatory constraints on synthetic warmers touching production PII datasets (we recommend synthetic-only for compliance lane warmups).

If that looks reasonable, can we lock the pilot dates and get ops to approve the rack reservation? I propose Dec 13–27 for the sandbox window.

Attachments: lane-allocations-v1.csv, network-egress-model.pdf

Thanks,
Rishi

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-12-03T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy GPU pool capacity kickoff / info request

Team —

Good proposal. Approve the lane split with one adjustment: increase Lane C pinned capacity by one GPU-equivalent (to ensure KMS-backed audit throughput while we validate logs). That change should be accounted for in the pilot sizing and cost model.

Rishi — please update the lane CSV and pilot acceptance criteria (add a pass condition for audit log write latency < 200ms for compliance lane).

Priya — please confirm rack reservation for Dec 13 and that your ops team is OK with synthetic warmers and the pinned pre-warm approach. Once we have that, we’ll publish the kickoff doc and calendar invites.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Product — Private Deploy
Redwood Inference
